subject: Air-gapped on-prem qualification — hardware & upgrade playbook (recap)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@bioplux.com>, infra@bioplux.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Air-gapped on-prem qualification call — HW, upgrades, next steps

Hi Ethan / BioPlux infra team,

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so your team can validate before the SOW draft: 

1) Deployment mode decision
- Confirmed interest in Private (air-gapped on-prem) deployment (appliance image + on-site install) rather than Hosted API or Dedicated GPU pool.

2) Hardware baseline (what we need to validate)
- Rack space: 4U per Redwood appliance node (recommend 4 nodes to start).
- Power: dual 32A PDUs per rack, N+1 redundancy.
- Network: isolated management VLAN for out-of-band; no internet egress.
- Storage: 8 TB NVMe per node (RAID recommended), local SSD for KV cache.
- Spare kit: 1 spare GPU, 1 spare PSU, 2 spare NVMe drives (more details in HW checklist attachment).

3) Upgrade & patching model
- Offline patch bundles: we provide signed patch bundles and an on-prem installer that runs from an encrypted USB or via airgap transfer.
- Quarterly security patch cadence recommended; emergency hotfixes as signed bundles.
- We need confirmation of acceptable maintenance window (proposed quarterly 4-hour window) and an on-call escalation path.

4) Observability & logs
- We will run local telemetry and produce audit logs that can be exported on request. For SOC/forensics, we provide an evidence export procedure (manual, secure copy).

5) On-site support & training
- Optional on-site install and operator training (2 days).
- Runbook handover + runbook access link included in attachments.

Action items / next steps
- BioPlux: validate rack/power/storage numbers and confirm maintenance window acceptability (reply to this thread).
- Redwood: produce SOW draft + procurement checklist and propose DocuSign link once BioPlux confirms PO flow.

Attachments: redwood-airgap-sow-v0.3.pdf, hw-checklist-bioplux.xlsx (hardware ask table); internal runbook link shared below.

I’ve looped in Marissa (solutions) to clarify the offline install and spare part flow. Thanks — Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@bioplux.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@bioplux.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Air-gapped on-prem qualification call — HW, upgrades, next steps

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side before we sign off for SOW: 

- Hardware numbers: the suggested 4 appliance nodes are fine (we're planning 3ᐟ1 HA). For power, we have dual 32A PDUs but need to surface exact breaker/cabling details to ops — I'll attach our rack worksheet.

- Upgrade cadence: quarterly 4-hour windows are acceptable for non-emergency updates. For emergency hotfixes, we need an option for an offline patch that our infra team can stage and apply with a documented rollback. Is that how the signed bundle works?

- Remote support: since there's zero egress, does Redwood provide encrypted USB images + verification checksums and a contact at install for secure handoff?

- Logs: we need a clear exportable evidence package for compliance: which logs are supported (audit, request traces, model artifacts?) and the expected retention we can configure locally.

- Procurement: we'll need a simple SOW and a DocuSign-ready contract. PO will be raised after SOW review. Our target on-site install week would be Apr 12 (ops availability permitting).

Please include Ben from procurement on the contract thread (ben@bioplux.com). I’ll share the rack worksheet shortly.

--
Ethan Cole
Head of Infrastructure, BioPlux Labs
ethan.cole@bioplux.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@bioplux.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Air-gapped on-prem qualification call — HW, upgrades, next steps

Ethan — quick technical follow-up from my side (solutions engineering). Short answers first, details below.

- Offline patch bundles: yes — signed tarballs + SHA256 checksums. We provide an install script that validates signatures before applying. Rollback: we create snapshot-based rollback instructions; we test the rollback procedure in our lab images and include the MOP in the runbook.

- Encrypted media: we can ship a FIPS 140-2 encrypted USB key for the initial appliance image and emergency patches. Each media is signed and we provide an install-verify utility.

- Logs / evidence package: supported exports include request traces (user id obfuscated), system audit logs, kernel logs, and model-serving traces for the last 30 days by default. Retention is configurable — we recommend 90 days for audit traces; longer retention can be configured to local NFS if required.

- Spare parts & firmware: we maintain an on-call spare-parts kit (1x GPU, 1x PSU, spare NVMe). Firmware coordination: we coordinate with your ops to push firmware updates during the agreed maintenance window; we do not push firmware without customer approval.

- Install & training: we recommend 2 days on-site for the initial install + 1 day operator workshop (runbook handover).

Pricing note: Private (air-gapped) deployments include an integration & packaging fee (one-time) + a private support tier. I’ll flag Brent in pricing if you want an estimate now — otherwise Jasmine will attach the SOW and baseline numbers.

Attachments: appliance-offline-install.md (step-by-step MOP), spare-parts-list.csv. Drive link to runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-redwood-airgap-runbooks

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm who will be the primary on-site operator (name and email)?
- Do you require us to inventory specific firmware versions for existing rack devices prior to install?

If you confirm the quarterly 4-hour maintenance window (any Fri 02:00–06:00 local), we’ll mark that preference in the SOW.

Best,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@bioplux.com>

Subject: Re: Recap: Air-gapped on-prem qualification call — HW, upgrades, next steps

Marissa / Jasmine — this all looks good and aligns with our security team’s expectations. Answers below: 

- Primary on-site operator: Priya Singh (priya.singh@bioplux.com) — she’ll be on-site for the install.
- Firmware inventory: yes please — we’ll collect current firmware/BIOS versions and share by Mar 24.
- Maintenance window: quarterly 4-hour window accepted (Fri 02:00–06:00 local).

Procurement: we’ll raise a PO after SOW review. PO number (internal): BPLX-PO-2027-1123 (attached). Please send the SOW and a DocuSign-ready contract; include estimated lead time for shipping encrypted USB + spare kit and the on-site week availability (we’d prefer week of Apr 12).

Ben (copied) will handle contract review on our side.

Thanks — looking forward to the SOW and next steps.
